title: Human kidney tubuloid cyst-induction imaging inventory
question: Can the public bright-field cyst-induction images support a reproducible, object-level phenotype analysis without confusing image fields with independent biological samples?

scope.model_system: Adult stem-cell-derived human kidney tubuloids cultured in collagen domes or suspension, with source images of forskolin, DMSO vehicle, and untreated conditions.
scope.claim_boundary: This is a source-image inventory for a disease-modeling study; there are no local segmentations or measurements, and image morphology does not demonstrate renal function, rejuvenation, or human benefit.

protocol.summary: The source article describes bright-field imaging at 5, 24, 48, and 72 hours after treatment and QuPath-based tracking and measurement. This repository record indexes 280 Figure 4 images; it does not reproduce the wet-lab procedure or the source annotations.
deviations: No culture, treatment, image segmentation, or biological assay was performed in this repository.
Individual tubuloid track identities are not present in the archive filenames or this source-image inventory.

design.intervention: 10 µM forskolin to activate chronic cAMP signaling, compared with DMSO vehicle and untreated medium across dome and suspension culture.
design.experimental_unit: Source culture replicate A, B, or C within a kidney, culture condition, and treatment; each unit can have multiple timepoint images.
design.independent_unit: Source kidney identifier for the frozen development/test partition; mapping to unique human donors is not established by this manifest.

donor_structure.notes: Five source kidney identifiers appear in the Figure 4 filenames. This inventory uses them to keep related images together but does not treat them as verified donor identities or estimate donor-level performance.

assays.name: Bright-field cyst morphology and object tracking
assays.endpoint: Per-object cyst area and longitudinal cyst change across the reported post-treatment imaging times.
assays.experimental_unit: Culture replicate with its image fields; individual tubuloids are not linked across images here.
assays.source_n: 280 indexed source images; 0 image masks measured, 280 pending annotation, 0 missing, 0 failed.
assays.notes: The linked intake indexed the source images but measured no masks. No cyst morphology or biological outcome is claimed.

validation_endpoints.rationale: Kidney function is not measured by these source bright-field images or by the current intake.
No cell-identity assay is linked to this Figure 4 image inventory.
Image morphology alone does not establish viability, and no linked viability values are in this record.
No genome-stability or off-target measurements are linked to this cyst-induction image inventory.
No linked adverse-effect assay is available in this source-image intake.
The indexed images do not provide verified object tracks or durable post-treatment function.

source_model.method: No segmentation or phenotype model has been fit; this record catalogs source images only.
source_model.reason: The archive contains images but no masks or annotation identities for a local evaluation.

donor_validation.split: Frozen holdout of one source kidney identifier; source IDs are not asserted to be unique donor IDs.
donor_validation.reason: No reviewed mask outcomes are available, and the mapping from the five source kidney IDs to independent human donors is not established in this analysis record.

modeling.falsifier: Any future image-based cyst-suppression claim should fail if blinded, reviewed object-level scoring does not reproduce the prespecified difference across held-out biological units.

calibration.notes: The archive metadata reports a 5x objective, but this intake has not validated pixel calibration for each image; physical morphology is not reported.

limitations: The image intake has 280 TIFF frames and no supplied instance masks; every frame remains pending annotation.
The source kidney identifier is used only to prevent split leakage; this manifest does not equate it with a unique donor.
Filename replicate letters identify source technical replicates, not individual tracked tubuloids.
The current case has no local segmentation benchmark, phenotype summary, or reproduced source measurement.
Cyst morphology in an in-vitro kidney disease model does not measure kidney function, general tissue regeneration, aging reversal, or human benefit.

developmental_context.interval_label: Adult stem-cell-derived kidney tubuloids; source images span 5–72 hours after culture treatment.
developmental_context.notes: This is an in-vitro adult kidney disease-model track, not embryonic development or gestational support.
